questions.prompt: All of the following are parts of a compound microscope EXCEPT: (i) eyepiece, (ii) objective, (iii) condenser, (iv) fine and coarse adjustment, (v) stage.
questions.explanation: All five items are parts of a compound microscope, so none of them is the exception.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following structures is unique to a prokaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleoid is the region where the prokaryotic DNA lies, with no nuclear membrane. Ribosomes occur in all cells, while the cytoskeleton and Golgi apparatus are eukaryotic.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which organelle breaks down fatty acids and produces hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and make hydrogen peroxide, which the enzyme catalase then breaks down.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which organelle is the site of aerobic cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and make most of the cell's ATP.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Options B–D were cut off in the typed paper and were replaced with standard alternatives.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of a typical plant cell?
questions.explanation: Higher plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole, but they lack centrioles.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Lipid synthesis and detoxification are carried out by the ________.
questions.explanation: Smooth ER (no ribosomes) makes lipids and detoxifies drugs and poisons. Rough ER makes proteins.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The gel-like substance inside the cell, excluding the nucleus, where cellular processes occur is the ________.
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the gel-like contents of the cell outside the nucleus, where most cell processes take place.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which organelles contain digestive enzymes to break down waste materials and cellular debris?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes hold hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes that break down worn-out organelles, wastes and engulfed material.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of these is common to animals, plants and fungi?
options: Ability to make their own food (autotrophy).
questions.explanation: Animals, plants and fungi are all eukaryotes, so their cells have a true nucleus. Animal cells have no cell wall, and only plants (with algae) are autotrophic.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of these is/are NOT correct about the cell?
options: Cellular processes occur in the cytoplasm.
PSI and PSII are producers of ATP/NADPH in the cell.
The nucleus is the control center of the cell.
Ribosomes are either floating in the cytosol or attached to the ER.
questions.explanation: Option B is probably intended, since photosystems exist only in photosynthetic cells (in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts), but the statement is loosely worded.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: The intended answer depends on the wording of option B. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a common component in all cells?
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane, ribosomes and cytoplasm are present in all cells. The cell wall is absent in animal cells.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: Three options are correct. Please confirm the intended answer.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a hydrolytic enzyme?
questions.explanation: Ribonuclease and amylase are both hydrolytic enzymes.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: Two options (B and C) are correct. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: The ________ were once thought to be fungi because of their branched mycelium, but are now known to be prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: Actinomycetes are filamentous bacteria that form branching, mycelium-like growth, so they were once classified with fungi.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements are NOT true about viruses? (i) They lack ribosomes. (ii) They contain both DNA and RNA. (iii) Outside the host cell, a non-living particle is called a virion. (iv) The central core is surrounded by a protein coat called a capsid. (v) They contain either DNA or RNA.
questions.explanation: A virus contains either DNA or RNA, never both, so statement (ii) is false. The others are true.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following are completely prokaryotic organisms?
questions.explanation: Bacteria (with archaea) are prokaryotes. Protozoa, algae and fungi are eukaryotes.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following has a cell wall containing peptidoglycan?
questions.explanation: Peptidoglycan is found in bacterial cell walls. Plant walls are cellulose and animal cells have no wall.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Choose the domain that contains primitive prokaryotes living in extreme environments.
questions.explanation: Archaea include extremophiles such as halophiles, methanogens and heat-loving species. (Protista is a kingdom, not a domain.)
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The club fungi and the sac fungi are also known as ________ and ________, respectively.
questions.explanation: Club fungi are Basidiomycota and sac fungi are Ascomycota.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT in the Kingdom Fungi?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium falciparum is the malaria parasite, a protist. The other three are fungi.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which organisms are mostly responsible for the decomposition of organic matter?
questions.explanation: Saprophytic fungi such as Trichoderma are the main decomposers. The other three groups mainly handle methane or nitrogen compounds.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Carrageenan, a mucilaginous polysaccharide from ________, is useful in making agar for culture media.
questions.explanation: Carrageenan comes from red algae (Rhodophyta), which are seaweeds, so both a and b are correct.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The algal divisions are classified based on all of the following criteria EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Algae are separated into divisions mainly by pigments, storage products and flagella (and cell wall), not by their mode of reproduction.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: A lion hunting a zebra is an example of ________.
questions.explanation: A predator kills and eats its prey.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Tapeworms living in a host's intestine are ________.
questions.explanation: Parasites that live inside the host are endoparasites.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Hermit crabs using empty gastropod shells demonstrate ________.
questions.explanation: In metabiosis one organism uses the remains or products of another (here an empty shell) without harming it.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a saprophytic organism?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms feed on dead and decaying matter.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the causative organism of trichomoniasis?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: In commensalism, the relationship is best described as:
options: One benefits, the other is harmed
One benefits, the other is unaffected
questions.explanation: In commensalism one partner benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: What kind of biological interaction exists when an organism hunts, kills and consumes another organism?
questions.explanation: That is predation.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Option A was printed as "Carnivory" in the original paper.

questions.prompt: What kind of interaction exists when Novomessor cockerelli uses small rocks to plug the entrance and hinder red harvester ants' foraging?
questions.explanation: Directly blocking a competitor from a resource is interference (contest) competition.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: To which parasite category does Plasmodium belong?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium lives inside red blood cells and liver cells, so it is an intracellular parasite.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Corals and zooxanthellae exhibit ________.
questions.explanation: The coral shelters the algae and the algae supply food from photosynthesis: mutualism.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: The typed question gave two pairs (corals and zooxanthellae, or sea anemones and hermit crabs); it now uses the first.

questions.prompt: ________ is a parasitic plant.
questions.explanation: Cuscuta (dodder) is a parasitic flowering plant. The other three are protozoan parasites.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: In which of the following habitats are parasites found?
questions.explanation: Parasites occur wherever their hosts live, so in all of these habitats.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Organisms of different species living together in close association in the same habitat exhibit ________.
questions.explanation: Symbiosis means living together in close association. (Interspecific interaction is the broader term for any interaction between species.)
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The relationship between the sea anemone and the clownfish can best be described as ________.
questions.explanation: The clownfish is protected by the anemone and cleans it and drives off predators: mutualism.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Option C was printed as "parasitoidism" in the original paper.

questions.prompt: Which of these best explains a "phoresy" relationship?
options: Temporary attachment of one organism to another for transportation
A relationship that involves direct interaction between individuals via aggression
Occurs when an organism competes for territory by being the first to occupy it
Both organisms depend entirely on each other for survival and cannot live independently
questions.explanation: In phoresy one organism hitches a ride on another for transport and does no harm.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of these causes an immune response in their host?
questions.explanation: Parasites live in or on a host and trigger its immune response.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: All of the following are saprotrophs EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fleas are blood-feeding parasites. Moulds, Bacillus and Pseudomonas feed on dead matter.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Saprotrophs have found applications in all of the following fields EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Saprotrophs are used in all three fields, so none is the exception.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Biotic interactions may be ________ or ________.
questions.explanation: Interactions are either within one species (intraspecific) or between species (interspecific).
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Options A and C were identical in the typed paper; option C was changed.

questions.prompt: Based on the species involved, competition can be ________.
questions.explanation: Competition is intraspecific (same species) or interspecific (different species).
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: ________ occurs when a resource used by one organism reduces the amount available to another.
questions.explanation: Exploitative competition is indirect: organisms compete by using up a shared resource.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Types of mutualism include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Inquilinism (living in the shelter of another species) is a type of commensalism.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: ________ is a type of commensalism in which one organism indirectly benefits from another species (for example by using its remains).
questions.explanation: Metabiosis is the use of another organism's remains or products.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The characteristics of organisms in a symbiotic relationship have developed ________.
questions.explanation: Long-term partners adapt to each other: co-evolution.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Parasites are ________.
questions.explanation: Parasites are usually kept distinct from predators, but ecologists often call them "micropredators".
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: The intended answer is arguable. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: An example of a one-sided metabolically dependent relationship is ________.
questions.explanation: Parasitism fits "metabolically dependent" best, but commensalism is also one-sided.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: The wording could fit parasitism or commensalism. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: ________ is a form of feeding in which organisms get their nutrients from dead and decaying organic substances.
questions.explanation: Saprophytism and saprophytic nutrition mean the same thing.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: Options A and D are the same. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: An appropriate term for the human resident flora (microbiota) is ________.
questions.explanation: Many resident microbes are commensals, but gut bacteria that help digestion are mutualists.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: Two options (A and D) can be defended. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: Which habitat is characterized by permafrost?
questions.explanation: The Arctic tundra has permanently frozen soil (permafrost) and low vegetation.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Coral reefs are examples of ________.
questions.explanation: Coral reefs are marine (sea) habitats.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The functional role of an organism in its environment is called its ________.
questions.explanation: A niche is the role an organism plays, including what it eats, where it lives and how it interacts. A habitat is the place.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: What term describes interaction between organisms of the same species?
questions.explanation: Intraspecific means within one species.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which biome has the highest net primary productivity?
questions.explanation: Among terrestrial biomes the tropical rainforest has the highest net primary productivity (warm, wet and sunny all year).
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Options B–D were cut off in the typed paper and were replaced with other biomes.

questions.prompt: The assemblage of individuals of the same species in a given area is called a ________.
questions.explanation: A population is a group of the same species living in one area.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which terrestrial habitat is the most biologically diverse?
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests hold the greatest diversity of species on land.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is associated with low temperatures, permafrost and limited vegetation?
questions.explanation: Arctic tundra is the cold biome with permafrost and sparse low plants.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: All of the following are characteristics of a boreal forest (taiga) EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The taiga is cold, northern and covered with conifers, with no tropical climate.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: In the natural system of classification, plants are classified based on: (i) their ultimate use, (ii) similarities and differences in morphological and reproductive characters, (iii) evolutionary relationships reflecting genetic relationships, (iv) all characters considered in deciding whether a plant is related to another.
questions.explanation: The natural system groups plants by overall similarity of form and reproductive structures, using all characters. Grouping by evolutionary relationships is the phylogenetic system, and grouping by use is not a natural classification.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: In the Five Kingdom system, Actinomycetes and Cyanobacteria are placed in the kingdom ________, while Ulothrix and Acetabularia are placed in the kingdom ________.
questions.explanation: Actinomycetes and cyanobacteria are prokaryotes (Monera). As taught in this course, the algae Ulothrix and Acetabularia go in Protista.
questions.source: BOT 101, April 2019 and BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The lowest major rank in the classification hierarchy is ________.
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest of the major ranks.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The system of binomial nomenclature is associated with ________.
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature (genus and species names).
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following shows the correct hierarchical classification from highest to lowest?
questions.explanation: Going down the hierarchy: Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a valid biological binomial name?
questions.explanation: Each is a genus name followed by a species epithet, so all three are valid binomial names.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Species are found among ________.
questions.explanation: All living organisms are grouped into species.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a Protist?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a yeast (a fungus). The others are protists.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Zea mays (maize) is a plant. The others are mammals (rat, mouse, lion, horse).
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The highest taxonomic rank is the ________, followed by ________.
questions.explanation: The order is Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Life is currently divided into three domains, namely ________, ________ and ________.
questions.explanation: The three domains are Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The classification of organisms is important for all of the following reasons EXCEPT:
options: it provides an unequivocal, unique name for organisms
it improves the ability to explain relationships
it reveals order and harmony between organisms as originally pre-planned by God
questions.explanation: Modern classification is a scientific tool for naming and relating organisms. It does not rest on a claim of pre-planned order.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The ________ system is the system of classification based on similarities and differences in morphological and reproductive characters.
questions.explanation: That describes the natural system.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT describe the growth habit of a plant?
questions.explanation: Herb, shrub and tree are growth habits. A tuber is a storage organ.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Modern classification of organisms incorporates all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The doctrine of signatures was an old belief that a plant's shape shows its use. It is not part of modern classification.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of these is the correct scientific name of bread wheat?
questions.explanation: Bread wheat is Triticum aestivum. Oryza sativa is rice and Zea mays is maize.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Triticum vulgare is an old synonym of Triticum aestivum.

questions.prompt: Modern taxonomy incorporates various techniques to classify organisms EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: "Biological analysis" is not a specific technique, but phenotypic and morphological analysis overlap, so the intended answer is unclear.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: The intended answer is unclear. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are members of the plant kingdom EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fungi are not plants. Algae also lie outside the plant kingdom in the five-kingdom system taught in this course.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: Options C and D were partly cut off in the typed paper and both may be correct. Needs the original paper.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a member of Kingdom Plantae? (options partly cut off)
questions.explanation: Amoeba proteus is a protozoan, so it is not a plant. The other options were cut off.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: Options B–D are missing. Needs the original paper.

questions.prompt: The total of all chemical reactions within an organism is called ________.
questions.explanation: Metabolism is all chemical reactions in an organism, building up (anabolism) and breaking down (catabolism).
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: ________ reproduction results in genetic variation and diversity among organisms.
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents, so offspring vary.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which one of these does NOT distinguish a living organism from a non-living entity?
questions.explanation: Living things respond to stimuli (they are sensitive). Insensitivity does not distinguish living things.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a reproductive strategy?
questions.explanation: Parental care, semelparity (breeding once), iteroparity (breeding repeatedly) and seasonal breeding are all reproductive strategies.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT an asexual means of reproduction?
questions.explanation: All four are asexual means of reproduction.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Maintenance of a stable internal environment despite external changes is called ________.
questions.explanation: That is homeostasis.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Cell division that halves the chromosome number, giving four daughter cells, is ________.
questions.explanation: Meiosis gives four cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of non-living things?
questions.explanation: Excretion, reproduction, respiration and feeding are all characteristics of living things, so none of them is a characteristic of non-living things.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: All of the following are advantages of sexual reproduction EXCEPT:
options: only one type of sex cell is involved
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction needs two types of gamete (male and female). Having only one type of sex cell is not an advantage of it.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The metabolic processes that build up complex materials from simpler ones are called ________.
questions.explanation: Anabolism builds complex molecules from simple ones. Catabolism breaks them down.
questions.source: BIO 101, September 2024 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Sexual reproduction involves all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fertilization, gamete formation and meiosis are steps of sexual reproduction. Mitosis is part of development after fertilization and is also the basis of asexual reproduction.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: The intended answer (mitosis) is arguable, because mitosis is involved in development. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: Understanding ________, from cellular processes to complex behaviors, gives insight into the diversity of life and the perpetuation of genetic information across generations.
questions.explanation: The wording could point to reproduction or to evolution.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.reviewNote: The intended answer is unclear. Please confirm.

questions.prompt: ________ is a double-helix molecule that encodes genetic instructions.
questions.explanation: DNA is the double-helix molecule that carries the genetic code.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Different forms of a gene found at the same locus on homologous chromosomes are called ________.
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene at the same locus.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following was NOT a key trait in Mendel's studies on pea genetics?
questions.explanation: Mendel studied seed shape and colour, pod shape and colour, flower colour and position, and stem height, but not stem colour.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: All of the following are reasons why Pisum sativum was ideal for Mendel's experiments EXCEPT:
options: having both male and female reproductive organs
questions.explanation: Nitrogen fixation was not a reason. Peas are easy to grow, can be self- or cross-pollinated and have bisexual flowers.

questions.prompt: For a test cross to be effective, one of the parents must be a known ________.
questions.explanation: A test cross uses a homozygous recessive parent, so the offspring show the genotype of the other parent.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is UNTRUE?
options: The Y chromosome is relatively gene-poor.
Males are only able to inherit their father's sex-linked traits.
Male grasshoppers have an X chromosome but no Y chromosome.
Male birds have a ZZ chromosome pair.
questions.explanation: A male inherits his X chromosome (and so X-linked traits) from his mother. Only Y-linked traits come from the father. The other statements are true.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)
questions.sourceNote: Option D was printed as "XX" in the original; male birds are ZZ.

questions.prompt: ________ are long, thread-like structures composed of DNA and proteins.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are thread-like structures of DNA wrapped around proteins.

questions.prompt: When were the key hereditary experiments of Correns, Tschermak and Hugo de Vries conducted?
questions.explanation: The three men rediscovered Mendel's work in 1900, years after Mendel died (1884).
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct pairing of nucleotide bases in DNA?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and cytosine pairs with guanine.

questions.prompt: The haploid number of chromosomes in Loxodonta africana (African bush elephant, 2n = 56) is ________.
questions.explanation: The haploid number is half the diploid number: 56 ÷ 2 = 28.
questions.source: BIO 101, June 2025 (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard textbook knowledge)

questions.prompt: The diploid number of chromosomes in Homo sapiens is ________.
questions.explanation: Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

questions.prompt: The chromosomal abnormality with an XXY constitution is ________.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the nucleotide bases in DNA?

questions.prompt: All of the following are sex-linked (or sex-influenced) traits EXCEPT:

questions.prompt: Where is genetic information encoded?

questions.prompt: Common variations in DNA sequence that occur in a population without necessarily affecting health or development are known as ________.
